newsitem.title: UK: Zinc pushes higher on LME, others do little.
newsitem.headline: Zinc pushes higher on LME, others do little.

text.p: Zinc prices moved higher during Wednesday pre-market LME trading, comfortably regaining the $1,500 a tonne level.
Other markets were trading fairly routinely, ahead of the August traded option declarations which take place from 1000 GMT onwards.
"Zinc has been active - good two-way business - but the others are pretty quiet," one trader said.

Zinc ranged up from just under $1,500 to touch $1,511, a $13 advance from Tuesday's overnight kerb close. Short-covering amd some Far Eastern buying was reasonably well absorbed by speculative sales overhead.

Wednesday's stock fall of 575 tonnes, following two days of inventory increases, augmented the upmove. Traders said there should be support now just above $1,500, while a $10 widening in the backwardation to $80/90 was also supportive. There is resistance expected around $1,520.
Elsewhere, copper drifted back from steadier late Tuesday levels, but was constrained within a narrow range, reflecting the current technical impasse.

Stocks rose by 4,300 tonnes, but this was not unexpected, given the summer slowdown and recent squeeze. Three months was holding at $2,300, up $14 from the previous kerb, but still slightly down from the $2,307/10 late close.

Aluminium traded routinely between $1,732 and $1,727, up $6 from the overnight kerb, with the market cautious ahead of option declarations. Key strikes are said to be at $1,500 and $1,500, with the August date in the middle of these at present.
Lead clawed its way higher, trying to recover from Tuesday's fall to 22-month lows of $598. Business was at $610, up $5.
Nickel was $10 higher at $7,270, but tin was indicated at a slightly softer $5,560/70. Alloy was stable at $1,520/30.
